children: Festive demand propelled India’s electric two-wheeler registrations to an all-time monthly peak of 2,23,886 units in October, surpassing the previous high of 2,19,724 units recorded during the festive season in October 2024 by 1.9 per cent. Registrations also rose 8.4 per cent from 2,06,500 units in October last year, highlighting the market’s expansion even as competition intensified among manufacturers.

The latest tally was 7.3 per cent higher than September’s 2,08,707 units, the previous peak for 2026, and 8.7 per cent above July’s 2,05,885 units. October was the third month this year that electric two-wheeler registrations crossed two lakh units, according to Vahan data.

But beneath the festive record, the competitive order is shifting. TVS Motor Company widened its lead over Bajaj Auto, Hero MotoCorp closed in on Ather Energy, and Ola Electric continued to lose ground. More significantly, electric two-wheeler penetration declined to 9.65 per cent from 11.58 per cent in September as conventional two-wheelers grew faster.
Natural Choice

Hemant Kabra, Founder and Managing Director of BGauss Electric, said the all-time peak in electric two-wheeler registrations reflects a broader shift in consumer preferences, with more buyers recognising the economic benefits of electric mobility amid global energy uncertainty.

“The record registrations show that electric two-wheelers are increasingly becoming a natural choice for Indian consumers. With global uncertainties keeping energy costs and fuel-price volatility in focus, customers are recognising the benefits of lower running costs, predictable ownership expenses and reduced dependence on petrol. This shift is no longer confined to early adopters but is gradually becoming part of mainstream mobility,” Kabra said.

BGauss Electric registered 5,554 electric two-wheelers in October, up 10.5 per cent from 5,024 in September, outperforming the overall market’s 7.3 per cent growth. The October tally was just six units below its July peak of 5,560 registrations, while cumulative registrations during January–October stood at 40,724 units.
TVS widens lead
TVS Motor retained electric two-wheeler leadership for the tenth consecutive month, registering 60,433 units in October, an 11.1 per cent increase from 54,404 in September.
Its lead over second-placed Bajaj Auto more than doubled to 11,365 units from 5,662, the widest monthly gap between the two manufacturers during January–October.

Bajaj’s registrations edged up just 0.7 per cent to 49,068 units from 48,742, reducing its market share to 21.92 per cent from 23.35 per cent. TVS increased its share to 26.99 per cent from 26.07 per cent.
Hero closes in on Ather

The contest for third place tightened as Hero MotoCorp’s registrations jumped 22.5 per cent to 29,936 units from 24,441 in September, compared with Ather Energy’s 2.7 per cent increase to 31,795 units from 30,945.
Ather’s lead over Hero consequently shrank to just 1,859 units from 6,504 a month earlier.

TVS and Hero together contributed 11,524 additional registrations, accounting for nearly 76 per cent of the industry’s net monthly increase of 15,179 units. Hero’s market share climbed to 13.37 per cent from 11.71 per cent.
Ola loses further ground
Ola Electric’s registrations declined for a fourth consecutive month, falling 10.1 per cent to 12,096 units from 13,458 in September. Its market share slipped to 5.40 per cent from 6.45 per cent.
Greaves Electric Mobility registered 10,838 units, up 16.3 per cent from 9,319, narrowing Ola’s lead to just 1,258 units from 4,139.
River’s registrations rose 20.3 per cent to 6,796 units, also outperforming the broader electric two-wheeler market.
EV penetration slips

Total two-wheeler registrations jumped 28.7 per cent to 23,20,139 units in October, compared with electric two-wheeler growth of 7.3 per cent. Non-electric registrations increased 31.5 per cent, indicating that conventional motorcycles and scooters captured a larger share of festive demand.
During January–October, electric two-wheeler registrations reached 17,96,566 units, accounting for 9.40 per cent of overall two-wheeler retail.
TVS led the ten-month market with 4,72,367 registrations, followed by Bajaj at 4,03,459, Ather at 2,93,834, Hero at 2,02,685 and Ola at 1,20,027.
Growth outlook

Kranthi Bathini, Director–Equity Strategy at WealthMills Securities, said the rise in electric two-wheeler registrations reflects growing consumer acceptance, expanding product choices and improving distribution networks. However, the decline in penetration during the festive season suggests that conventional motorcycles and scooters continue to dominate the broader market recovery.

The industry’s next phase of growth will depend on manufacturers making electric vehicles more affordable, strengthening after-sales networks and building consumer confidence, particularly beyond major urban markets.

October’s all-time peak therefore underscores the expanding scale of India’s electric two-wheeler industry, even as competition intensifies and the faster growth of conventional vehicles highlights the challenge of translating higher electric sales into sustained market-share gains.

title: Festive cheer lifts electric two-wheeler retail to all-time peak of 2.24 lakh
